newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex cuts July Maya, raises Isthmus to Americas.
newsitem.headline: Pemex cuts July Maya, raises Isthmus to Americas.

text.p: Mexico cut its July price differentials for Maya crude oil to the Americas by 20 cents, and raised Isthmus crude to the Americas by 20 cents, a spokeswoman for state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said on Monday.

Pemex term crude contract prices are based on formulas comprised of weighted price ratios of crudes and products in the region with a constant, or differential, which is generally updated monthly to reflect market conditions.

The spokeswoman, who declined to be named, said Pemex did not change its differentials for ultra-light Olmeca crude in July to the Americas. It also left unchanged its prices for Isthmus and Maya crudes to Europe, she said.
For customers in the Far East, Maya price differentials were raised 15 cents while the price for Isthmus was left unchanged.
For current worldwide crude oil contract prices, please type OSP/O f9 on the Reuter's terminal.

In May Mexico sold Maya to the Americas at an average $15.20 per barrel, Isthmus at an average $18.23 and Olmeca at an average $19.42. To Europe, prices averaged about $13.02 for Maya and $17.44 for Isthmus in May. Sales to the Far East in May were at about $15.50 per barrel of Maya and $19.30 per barrel of Isthmus.
((--Timna Tanners, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7903. E-mail at timna.tanners@reuters.com))
